M O R E   M A I L ! !


  January, 1991      Page Reply

 Bob Bates............02    03
 Raymond Hoy..........04    07
 Leif Mortensen.......08    13
 D.P. Tucker..........15    17
 D.J. Wood............19    24
 K.P.A. Bates.........26    29
 Mark Payne...........30    31
 Mike Pike............32    35
 Stan Greenwood.......36    42

From Bob Bates

Dear Ron & Brian,

In reply to David Woods' enquiry
about repair of the Wafa drive
in Issue 41, I doubt if anyone
will repair them now but new
Wafa Drives have been on sale
at several recent All Formats
Shows including the last one in
Birmingham. The price was about
`10 or `15.Spare Wafas were also
on sale, complete with Spectral
Writer, for about `3.

Unfortunately I cannot remember
the name of the supplier and the
complete lack of service from
the organizer in the form of a
SHOWGUIDE provides nothing to
jog my memory.      - Bob Bates

To Mr Bates from Brian Gaff

It is certainly not worth
getting Wafadrives repaired, as
they seem to be very cheap at
the shows. Like you, I do not
know who had them, though the
name Graham Scarre springs to
mind.I would ring the organisers
and ask. They seem helpful.

I asked about showguides, but
the problem is one of time. With
shows so frequent, there is
often just not enough time to
correlate all the information,
and get it printed before a
show. From what I gather, the
London shows often have the
widest choice of goods on sale.

                        Brian G.

From: Raymond Hoy, BASINGSTOKE

Dear Brian and Ron,

I feel I must write to you and
your readers regarding a review
I read and responded to in
CHECKOUT (Issue 51).  As I use
PCG's desk top publishing prog-
rams combined with your clip art
(a great combination)I felt some
more clip art would be useful.

This letter is, I am afraid, a
complaint, i.e., the article
reviews PCG's clip art discs (3
altogether for `10). A bargain,
I thought, until they arrived
and I viewed them. To my horror
and disgust, to say I wasn't
happy is putting it mildly.

All the clip art I have been
getting from 'OUTLET' since you
have been putting it in were on
these discs that I have paid `10
for. Surely Brian Cooper (the
reviewer) has OUTLET and knows
this so why were readers not
warned? (It couldn't be he has a
vested interest, could it?) I
could not agree more with Brian
that they are good value for the
money but not if you have them
already. How many other readers
have been caught out by this?

On phoning PCG I asked how two
companies can be allowed to
publish the same thing i.e.,
yourself and them. I was told
because it was public domain.
This doesn't seem very fair to
the customer. What do you think?

Anyway they will be sent back
and I will ask for a refund.

Does anyone know if "Teachers
Pet" clip art discs has this
same problem or where else we
can obtain clip art that has not
been published by anyone else.

While in a moaning mood, did you
know that the Bingo program you
published (Issue 50) doesn't
work properly i.e., all cards
after the first one are printed
the same - not that any of your
readers would be interested in
Bingo anyway.

What a packed issue No.51 was,
so much so I could not get my
system on the disc (not a moan).
    Yours sincerely, RAYMOND HOY

Brian Cavers to Raymond Hoy

I'm sorry about the clip art
problem,Ray. That's why I raised
the subject in last month's
editorial but unfortunately too
late for you! There's more on
this matter from Leif Mortensen
in the next OUTLETTER. Some of
the 'Teachers Pet' clip art has
also been in OUTLET but not all.

The problem with BINGO should be
cured by inserting RANDOMIZE at
the start of line 340.I have not
had a chance to test this but it
should work. It is likely that I
introduced the fault myself when
I included our Spectrum OUTLET
printer dump routine which sets
RND to the same value every time
a card is dumped!        - Brian

From:Leif Mortensen, DENMARK

Well I simply have to come with
a comment to your editorial in
Issue 52 before anyone claims I
have been stealing any software
and claimed it to be mine. I see
you are surprised (seems to me
from your comment) that the CLIP
ART collection is alike from PCG
and the ones you are using.There
is one simple reason: they are
from me!

I sent PCG the first four C60
tapes as I had been asking a
couple of times about clips to
use with WORDMASTER, which I use
for my magazine, but he said
that he would NOT be making any
but I was of course welcome to
send it if I found any.

Then, one of my club members
found a way to transfer clips
from PC discs to the Spectrum
and so we transferred a lot of
small clips and cut it into 6K
bits which then was put onto
audio tapes. PCG has only got
the first four C60 tapes.

That also goes for the +3 User
Group with which I'm a little
cross -as soon as he had got the
clip art he was not interested
in sending me anything any more,
so I, of course, didn't send him
(+3 Group) any more. Another
thing is that he has been
selling the clip art for his
customers at large prices and
with less screens on - can you
call that PUBLIC DOMAIN?

ALL the PD programs YOU get from
me are carefully chosen among a
lot of programs from our PD
library (for Sam we have over 60
discs with various stuff) which
is placed with Thorsten Gudmund-
sen. Spectrum PD is placed by
me. No worry about using PD from
SINCLAIR FREAKEREN - if I'm not
sure I won't send it! Now a
couple of questions:

1. Are there any of your members
who knows anything about the
radio amateur scene? I have a
couple of RTTY enthusiasts who
would like to know of firms
selling anything for the ZX
Spectrum which can be used for
FAX satellite pictures a.s.o.
Please send any information to
the address below.

2. Has anybody knowledge of a
firm still supporting the
APRICOT 16 bit computer from
ACT? If anyone has a manual we
can buy,one of my members will
be glad.

3. Is there any firm in England
which will sell ink to my small
computer firm for my wet ribbon
re-inker? It has to be on trade
terms.

4. Toner for CANON photo copiers
is needed too - know of any firm
selling that?

Send any information to:

Leif Mortensen, Bryggervangen 29
DK 7120 Vejle 0st DENMARK

PS. Know that I've been with you
almost since the beginning; I
must say it's a shame to see a
letter complaining about the
price of OUTLET [Marc Broster,
OUTLETTERS 52].You are producing
an excellent mag at a discount
price!
         Yours friendly

         Leif Mortensen

Brian Caver to Leif Mortensen

Thanks, Leif.

I would not have been surprised
that PCG had the same PD art as
we had - only that our reviewer
wasn't aware of it. I have never
had any doubt about the validity
of your source and that this PD
material may be freely provided
by any company.

Several of our readers are radio
hams and hopefully someone may
contact you. I will also keep an
eye out for the Apricot manual
you mentioned. The only ribbon
re-inking firm I know of is
ALADDINK (address in earlier
OUTBOARDS). Perhaps they might
help?

Again, I'll keep a look out for
anyone advertising CANON toner.
Perhaps a large stationer's
advert in COMPUTER SHOPPER might
be fruitful.

Can anyone else help?

I've arranged your subscription
to keep going, Leif so don't
worry!
                        - Brian

From D.P. Tucker, KETTERING

Dear Sir,

 RE: CHECKOUT Review by Brian
 Cooper on Clip-art on disk from
 P.C.G. in OUTLET 51.


Before placing my order with PCG
I phoned them first to query the
price of this package for the
PLUS 3 on 3" disk. I was told
that clip art is ONLY supplied
on 3.5" disks and not at all for
the PLUS 3. Please could you
bring this to the attention of
any other OUTLET user with a
PLUS 3 who may be thinking of
sending for this clip art from
P.C.G.

Also, with the supply of 3"
disks maybe soon to come to an
end can you recommend a suitable
3.5" drive and power supply that
could be used as drive 'B' on
the PLUS 3?

              Thank you

             D. P. Tucker.

To Mr. Tucker from Brian Gaff

Though Amstrad have ceased hand-
ling 3" discs, Hitachi-Maxell
say they will continue to
manufacture them. Obviously,
there will come a day when this
will stop but I think in the
short term, our main worry will
be the price.

As has been stated here before,
most standard 3.5" 720K drives
will work on the +3. The points
to bear in mind are these.

It must be self powered.
The drive must be set internally
as drive 1, not drive 0.
The correct connector should be
on the cable.

The likelihood is that a disc
will need to be in the drive for
the +3 to see that it exists.
Any old duff disc will do. You
then use BFORMAT (OUTLET 48) and
there you are, 706K with 256
directory entries.       - B.G.

If you have trouble finding a
supplier anywhere you might
consider the UNIVERSAL drive at
`75+`3 pp from EEC LTD., 18-21
Misbourne House, Chiltern Hill,
Chalfont St. Peter, Bucks, SL9
9UE (Tel: 0753 888866).You'd get
one a bit cheaper if you scour
the adverts in say, PC magazines
etc. or go to an ALL-FORMATS
FAIR.However, EEC also do a lead
for `10 (+`6 pp!!!) so check if
this is included in the `75!
                          - B.C.

From: Dave Wood, CAMBRIDGE

Dear Brian,

From OUTLET 16 Outletters - is
there any further news of INDUG?
I can't get any response. I
would like a copy of 'conversion
TASWORD +2 to DATEL +D'.

Re:Brian Gaffs' edgecard circuit
(OUTLET 16)to enable the inter-
facing of a Spectrum +3 to +D,
have you a copy of the circuit
or could I write to Mr. Gaff?

I got the +3 broken at a boot
sale and it now works fine -
needed a new disc drive belt.
Now that the 3" discs are down
in price it is more attractive.

I have a Spectrum +2, Datel +D
and Multiface 1. The Multiface
and +D are not compatible and
cause the system to crash. I
have been able to get all three
to work together so that a
program can be loaded from
disc:- the +D switches OUT, the
multiface IN and then any
jiggery pokery can be performed
at will - programs then can be
ouput back to disc or tape etc.

It's very simple to implement,
needs a tiny switch, two short
lengths of wire and a soldering
iron. Take the top off the +D:-
on the circuit board edge
connector counting from the left
top No.15, (MREQ); unsolder the
pin of the edge connector from
the board.

Bend up slightly so that it no
longer makes contact. Solder 1
wire to the lifted pin, the
other to the board where the pin
came from. Solder the switch
across the wires and mount the
switch neatly on/in the top of
box. It works well.[We accept no
responsibility for this! - BC]

I'll be pleased to help readers
who haven't the bits to do the
job for the cost of the return
postage and parts. (A `1 book of
stamps would do).

Probably someone out there is
going to write in saying that if
you PEEK-POKE etc you can do the
same but my skills run in the
area of metalwork and solder!

Have you noticed the unpleasant
tendency in some of the Spectrum
magazines to rip off the younger
readers (or their parents) with
premium rate phone calls, enter
competitions or even worse
'free' programs that don't run
unless you enter a password -
"Get the password by ringing
0839" etc.

How about that for exploitation!

On a more pleasant note have you
noticed how cheap the Z80 CPU
has become?

N.R. Baldwell, 288 Eccleshall
Road, Sheffield (0742 552886)
are offering them for 60p! The
voltage regulator costs 75p!

The Z80 restored a little girl's
48K to health when she plugged a
Z81 16k rampack in, thinking it
was for a joystick - a bit of
careful soldering and joy all
round.

Have a nice Christmas

Please keep up the good work.

            Dave Wood

Brian Cavers to Dave Wood

I'm not sure how you could get
in touch with INDUG. They tend
to do all communication by tele-
phone.You could try ringing them
on 0452 412572 but I believe it
is limited to certain hours of
the day as a "hotline". In any
event, you would probably need
to join them to be eligible to
buy the software.

The device you need to enable a
+D to work on a +3 is THE FIXIT,
`9.50 - see B.G. SERVICES in
OUTBOARD. The circuit diagram is
not available for sale.Note that
Datel do TWO versions of the +D,
one of which INCLUDES a device
to let it work on a +3. I assume
you have the normal type!

Note that the +D will only work
on the +3 in 48K mode.Brian Gaff
assures me that if the FIXIT is
not satisfactory he will give
you a refund.

Thanks for the info on getting
a Multiface and +D together. It
sounds as if you are nearly
there if you can isolate the +D
with a switch! However, I am
surprised you can SAVE to the +D
using a Multiface 1.

                        - Brian

From: P.A. Bates, SIDCUP

Dear Ron and Brian,

You may remember I wrote to you
many issues ago about getting
work into print and the various
print options open to us.  Well,
you may have used or seen the
latest printer style on the
market - the bubble jet printer.

We have at work one of the most
sophisticated bubble jet colour
printers around. The "iris" ink
jet printer, this machine,
driven by whisper-based
mainframe computers through a
simple 286 pc gives one of the
best quality colour pre-proof
pictures I have ever seen.

The iris consists of a large
revolving drum down on which the
sub-straite, (paper to you), is
stuck and, as it spins, four ink
jets travel on a carriage along
the length of the paper. The
four inks: cyan, magenta, yellow
and black drop onto the paper or
are deflected by a shield which
moves into and out of position
many times a second.


The software which drives this
machine can,of course,be altered
to give different results for
different printing processes or
for different papers or can give
more than one copy, you can fit
about four A4 copies at one
time.

The main difference between this
ink jet system and conventional
systems is the image itself. You
may remember I told you that
images were made up of dots with
the heavier dots carrying the
most ink and appearing darker in
shade. Well, this new system has
no dots but the different shades
of colour are made by how many
times the deflector shield moves
in front of the jets and how
long it actually stays in place.

The biggest drawback is hardware
has to be kept scrupulously
clean at all times and of course
no b*!#!* ever wants to clean
it! There is so much happening
on the professional DTP front
that it is very hard to keep up
with it all.          P.A.BATES

Brian Cavers to K.P.A. Bates

Sounds good! I bet it cost a lot
though. Why not send us a sample
printout just for interest?

                        - Brian

From: Mark Payne, COVENTRY

Dear Sirs,

I am writing this letter to you
to say how much I have enjoyed
your OUTLET software.  I have
just become a member and
although I started with No.045 I
have found every one to be 100%
useful.  I will, in the near
future, have some more back
issues off you but in the mean-
time keep up the excellent
quality of your software club.

I am sorry if I have not sent my
first letter in the correct form
but as I send more and more I'll
no doubt get the hang of it.

                     MARK PAYNE

Brian Cavers to Mark Payne

Thanks, Mark! We accept letters
in any form but it saves time
and money if they are supplied
as textfiles and not just hand-
written or printed and Tasword
2 set at 32 columns is ideal.

                        - Brian

From: Mike Pike, NORTHALLERTON

I've finally bought a +D inter-
face for my trusty Speccy. The
drive,which I bought separately,
is in a beige metal case with
plastic feet and, although the
maker's name has been removed,it
would appear to be identical to
a Citizen drive. It may come as
a surprise, therefore, that it
only cost `29 inc. postage. It's
in perfect working order and
not a scratch on the case.

The reason for the cheapness is
that it is an "end of line" deal
from Hobbykit of London NW9
(081) 205 7485. They regularly
advertise bits of, and for, PC
clones in Everyday Electronics
magazine.

But be warned- there is no power
supply for this price! I made my
own, being reasonably competent
with electronics.

The one thing I find frustrating
about the +D is the licence
agreement to be signed before
Datel will send the goods.Faxing
instead of posting it back can
save time though, if you have a
machine at work you can use.

Many thanks to Bob Bates who
suggested several sources for
adventure solutions -I am trying
them now. Curiously enough, the
address and editor's name given
for Adventure Probe magazine is
the same as the 3D Construction
Kit User Group!

I didn't think 3D modelling had
much to do with dungeons and
dragons but I may be wrong! On
the subject of 3D Kit, I find
object selection very frustrat-
ing. Every object is assigned a
type name (cube, pyramid, etc.)
and a number. In order to
manipulate an object you have
already created, you have to
pick it from a list of all the
objects in that area using only
these two factors.

Unless you have a rough sketch
of your own with the object
numbers noted down, it is like
trying to find a program on a +D
disk given only the program
numbers and the type (BASIC,
CODE, etc.).

The 16-bit versions allow you to
point at the object you want.
Perhaps this is too complicated
for the Spectrum, but it would
be nice to at least assign a
unique name to each object as it
is created.

Anyway, keep up the good work on
Outlet. The Spectrum may
disappear as far as Amstrad are
concerned but I reckon it'll be
around for some time yet.
                          - MIKE

Thanks, Mike. It's a miracle the
3D kit fits a Spectrum anyway so
I guess we must forgive extras
in other versions! And yes, the
3D games ARE adventures but they
are graphical rather than text!
                         - Brian.

From: S.W. Greenwood,N.YORKSHIRE

Dear Sir,

Since receiving my batch of
OUTLETS I have not had time to
evaluate them in depth but I am
impressed with what I have seen
so far; a very professional
presentation.

I recently received a batch of
second-hand microdrive cart-
ridges which I bought through
MicroMart. Some were blank but
one had September '91 OUTLET on,
albeit somewhat corrupted. I
managed to read the letters
feature and I noted an enquiry
about a PAL programmer for the
Spectrum.

Your reply also stated that you
didn't really unerstand the
question and asked for clarifi-
cation; here it is.

PAL stands for Programmable
Logic Array and is, as its name
implies, an integrated circuit
with a number of logic gates
forming an array. To use this to
implement a logic function one
needs to program it by blowing
fuses, which are Links with the
chip. One keeps the Links one
needs and blows the Links one
does not need.

It belongs in the same family of
devices as the ULA (uncommitted
Logic Array) whose name, in view
of the previous remarks,is self-
explanatory.

It is a block of generalised
logic which,in its virgin state,
is uncommitted to any particular
function.It needs to be program-
med to perform a specific task.
These devices can replace a
whole batch of gates and flip-
flops, and bring a measure of
programmability into discrete
logic design.


I hope that this clarifies the
matter for you. It is a subject
I know a deal about as I am an
electronics design engineer, and
I spent many years designing
circuits and systems for
electronic control in automation
and instrumentation.

I am now unemployed and, because
I am almost retiring age,that is
not likely to change. However, I
keep myself amused and my brain
in gear with my Spectrum.


It started out as 16k but has
now got 48k, a proper keyboard,
and a proper PSU, which are the
two areas where corners were
cut. With those points taken
care of, I find it a very useful
machine indeed. In addition, I
use Betabasic which transforms
it into a first class unit.

I use it to play with Z80 code,
and to write programs for
circuit analysis and mathematics
which are my main interests.

Although I have been involved
with computers in one way or
another, from designing them to
using them in systems, since
1960, I had never had one of my
own until I got the Spectrum. I
have tried other machines, but
always come round to the view
that I can do everything I want
with what I've got.


To return to the PAL programmer
question,it would be technically
feasible to design one around a
Spectrum in the same way that
there have been designs for PROM
programmers but I can say with
reasonable confidence that this
has not been done as I think I
would have heard of it.

I have toyed with the idea of
producing some tutorial programs
on logic design along with a
method of simulating the logic,
therefore proving it before
building it. I thought that with
all the present-day "hype" about
IBM, and the widespread belief
among the majority that the
Spectrum is a kid's toy, that
nobody would take such a thing
seriously. However, it does seem
that there is a band of users
out there who recognise a good
thing when they see it.

        Yours sincerely,

         Stan Greenwood

Brian Cavers to Stan Greenwood

Many thanks for the explanation!
I now see a PAL is not the same
as PROM or EPROM memory;the main
difference being a PAL chip is
not blank to start with but is
pre-programmed with generalized
circuitry which is customized,as
you describe,by blowing fuses at
various places. Yes, that's new
to me and very interesting.Stick
around - your experience should
be useful to readers with hard-
ware queries - and why not share
your programs with us?

The SAM COUPE may also interest
you because Andy Wright's SAM
BASIC is BETABASIC with extra
features and the SAM is really a
"super-Spectrum".       - Brian.

From Bob Bates

Dear Ron & Brian,

In reply to David Woods' enquiry about repair of the Wafa drive in Issue 41, I doubt if anyone will repair them now but new Wafa Drives have been on sale at several recent All Formats Shows including the last one in Birmingham. To Mr Bates from Brian Gaff

It is certainly not worth getting Wafadrives repaired, as they seem to be very cheap at the shows. Like you, I do not know who had them, though the name Graham Scarre springs to mind.I would ring the organisers and ask. They seem helpful.

From: Raymond Hoy, BASINGSTOKE

Dear Brian and Ron,

I feel I must write to you and your readers regarding a review I read and responded to in CHECKOUT (Issue 51).  As I use PCG's desk top publishing prog- rams combined with your clip art (a great combination)I felt some more clip art would be useful.

This letter is, I am afraid, a complaint, i.e., the article reviews PCG's clip art discs (3 altogether for `10). A bargain, I thought, until they arrived and I viewed them. To my horror and disgust, to say I wasn't happy is putting it mildly.

All the clip art I have been getting from 'OUTLET' since you have been putting it in were on these discs that I have paid `10 for. Surely Brian Cooper (the reviewer) has OUTLET and knows this so why were readers not warned? (It couldn't be he has a vested interest, could it?) I could not agree more with Brian that they are good value for the money but not if you have them already. How many other readers have been caught out by this?

On phoning PCG I asked how two companies can be allowed to publish the same thing i.e., yourself and them. I was told because it was public domain. This doesn't seem very fair to the customer. What do you think?

Anyway they will be sent back and I will ask for a refund.

Does anyone know if "Teachers Pet" clip art discs has this same problem or where else we can obtain clip art that has not been published by anyone else.

While in a moaning mood, did you know that the Bingo program you published (Issue 50) doesn't work properly i.e., all cards after the first one are printed the same - not that any of your readers would be interested in Bingo anyway.

What a packed issue No.51 was, so much so I could not get my system on the disc (not a moan). Yours sincerely, RAYMOND HOY

Brian Cavers to Raymond Hoy

I'm sorry about the clip art problem,Ray. That's why I raised the subject in last month's editorial but unfortunately too late for you! There's more on this matter from Leif Mortensen in the next OUTLETTER. Some of the 'Teachers Pet' clip art has also been in OUTLET but not all.

The problem with BINGO should be cured by inserting RANDOMIZE at the start of line 340.I have not had a chance to test this but it should work. It is likely that I introduced the fault myself when I included our Spectrum OUTLET printer dump routine which sets RND to the same value every time a card is dumped!        - Brian

From:Leif Mortensen, DENMARK

Well I simply have to come with a comment to your editorial in Issue 52 before anyone claims I have been stealing any software and claimed it to be mine. I see you are surprised (seems to me from your comment) that the CLIP ART collection is alike from PCG and the ones you are using.There is one simple reason: they are from me!

I sent PCG the first four C60 tapes as I had been asking a couple of times about clips to use with WORDMASTER, which I use for my magazine, but he said that he would NOT be making any but I was of course welcome to send it if I found any.

Then, one of my club members found a way to transfer clips from PC discs to the Spectrum and so we transferred a lot of small clips and cut it into 6K bits which then was put onto audio tapes. PCG has only got the first four C60 tapes.

That also goes for the +3 User Group with which I'm a little cross -as soon as he had got the clip art he was not interested in sending me anything any more, so I, of course, didn't send him (+3 Group) any more. Another thing is that he has been selling the clip art for his customers at large prices and with less screens on - can you call that PUBLIC DOMAIN?

Bend up slightly so that it no longer makes contact. Solder 1 wire to the lifted pin, the other to the board where the pin came from. Solder the switch across the wires and mount the switch neatly on/in the top of box. It works well.[We accept no responsibility for this! - BC]

Dear Ron and Brian,

You may remember I wrote to you many issues ago about getting work into print and the various print options open to us.  Well, you may have used or seen the latest printer style on the market - the bubble jet printer.

We have at work one of the most sophisticated bubble jet colour printers around. The "iris" ink jet printer, this machine, driven by whisper-based mainframe computers through a simple 286 pc gives one of the best quality colour pre-proof pictures I have ever seen.

The iris consists of a large revolving drum down on which the sub-straite, (paper to you), is stuck and, as it spins, four ink jets travel on a carriage along the length of the paper. The four inks: cyan, magenta, yellow and black drop onto the paper or are deflected by a shield which moves into and out of position many times a second.

The software which drives this machine can,of course,be altered to give different results for different printing processes or for different papers or can give more than one copy, you can fit about four A4 copies at one time.

The main difference between this ink jet system and conventional systems is the image itself. You may remember I told you that images were made up of dots with the heavier dots carrying the most ink and appearing darker in shade. Well, this new system has no dots but the different shades of colour are made by how many times the deflector shield moves in front of the jets and how long it actually stays in place.

The biggest drawback is hardware has to be kept scrupulously clean at all times and of course no b*!#!* ever wants to clean it! There is so much happening on the professional DTP front that it is very hard to keep up with it all.          P.A.BATES

From: S.W. Greenwood,N.YORKSHIRE

Dear Sir,

Since receiving my batch of OUTLETS I have not had time to evaluate them in depth but I am impressed with what I have seen so far; a very professional presentation.

I recently received a batch of second-hand microdrive cart- ridges which I bought through MicroMart. Some were blank but one had September '91 OUTLET on, albeit somewhat corrupted. I managed to read the letters feature and I noted an enquiry about a PAL programmer for the Spectrum.

Your reply also stated that you didn't really unerstand the question and asked for clarifi- cation; here it is.

PAL stands for Programmable Logic Array and is, as its name implies, an integrated circuit with a number of logic gates forming an array. To use this to implement a logic function one needs to program it by blowing fuses, which are Links with the chip. One keeps the Links one needs and blows the Links one does not need.

It belongs in the same family of devices as the ULA (uncommitted Logic Array) whose name, in view of the previous remarks,is self- explanatory.

It is a block of generalised logic which,in its virgin state, is uncommitted to any particular function.It needs to be program- med to perform a specific task. These devices can replace a whole batch of gates and flip- flops, and bring a measure of programmability into discrete logic design.

I hope that this clarifies the matter for you. It is a subject I know a deal about as I am an electronics design engineer, and I spent many years designing circuits and systems for electronic control in automation and instrumentation.

I am now unemployed and, because I am almost retiring age,that is not likely to change. However, I keep myself amused and my brain in gear with my Spectrum.

It started out as 16k but has now got 48k, a proper keyboard, and a proper PSU, which are the two areas where corners were cut. With those points taken care of, I find it a very useful machine indeed. In addition, I use Betabasic which transforms it into a first class unit.

I use it to play with Z80 code, and to write programs for circuit analysis and mathematics which are my main interests.

Although I have been involved with computers in one way or another, from designing them to using them in systems, since 1960, I had never had one of my own until I got the Spectrum. I have tried other machines, but always come round to the view that I can do everything I want with what I've got.

To return to the PAL programmer question,it would be technically feasible to design one around a Spectrum in the same way that there have been designs for PROM programmers but I can say with reasonable confidence that this has not been done as I think I would have heard of it.

I have toyed with the idea of producing some tutorial programs on logic design along with a method of simulating the logic, therefore proving it before building it. I thought that with all the present-day "hype" about IBM, and the widespread belief among the majority that the Spectrum is a kid's toy, that nobody would take such a thing seriously. However, it does seem that there is a band of users out there who recognise a good thing when they see it.

Yours sincerely,

Stan Greenwood

Brian Cavers to Stan Greenwood

I now see a PAL is not the same as PROM or EPROM memory;the main difference being a PAL chip is not blank to start with but is pre-programmed with generalized circuitry which is customized,as you describe,by blowing fuses at various places. Yes, that's new to me and very interesting.Stick around - your experience should be useful to readers with hard- ware queries - and why not share your programs with us?

The SAM COUPE may also interest you because Andy Wright's SAM BASIC is BETABASIC with extra features and the SAM is really a "super-Spectrum".       - Brian.

**От: P.A. Bates, SIDCUP**

Дорогие Ron и Brian,

Возможно, вы помните, я писал вам много выпусков назад о подготовке материалов к печати и различных доступных нам вариантах. Что ж, возможно, вы использовали или видели новейший тип принтеров на рынке — струйные принтеры (bubble jet).

У нас на работе есть один из самых сложных цветных струйных принтеров. Принтер "iris", работающий на основе мэйнфреймов, подключенных через простой 286 PC, дает одно из самых качественных цветных пробных изображений, которые я когда-либо видел.

"Iris" состоит из большого вращающегося барабана, на который наклеивается подложка (бумага, если говорить проще), и по мере вращения четыре струйных сопла перемещаются на каретке вдоль бумаги. Четыре чернила: голубой (cyan), пурпурный (magenta), желтый (yellow) и черный (black) попадают на бумагу или отклоняются экраном, который перемещается в нужное положение много раз в секунду.

Программное обеспечение, управляющее этой машиной, конечно, можно изменить для получения различных результатов при разных процессах печати или для разной бумаги, или для печати более чем одной копии — за один раз можно уместить около четырех копий формата A4.

Главное отличие этой струйной системы от обычных — само изображение. Возможно, вы помните, я говорил, что изображения состоят из точек, причем более крупные точки содержат больше чернил и кажутся темнее. В этой новой системе точек нет, а различные оттенки цвета создаются тем, сколько раз отклоняющий экран перемещается перед соплами и как долго он остается на месте.

Самый большой недостаток в том, что оборудование нужно содержать в идеальной чистоте, а, конечно, никто не хочет этим заниматься! На профессиональном фронте DTP происходит так много всего, что за всем этим очень трудно уследить.

P.A. BATES

**От: S.W. Greenwood, N. YORKSHIRE**

Дорогой сэр,

С момента получения моей партии OUTLET у меня не было времени оценить их глубоко, но я впечатлен тем, что увидел до сих пор; очень профессиональное оформление.

Недавно я получил партию подержанных картриджей Microdrive, которые купил через MicroMart. Некоторые были пустыми, но на одном был OUTLET за сентябрь '91, хотя и немного поврежденный. Мне удалось прочитать раздел писем, и я заметил вопрос о программаторе PAL для Spectrum.

Ваш ответ гласил, что вы не совсем поняли вопрос и попросили разъяснений; вот они.

PAL означает Programmable Logic Array (программируемая логическая матрица) и является, как следует из названия, интегральной схемой с рядом логических вентилей, образующих массив. Чтобы использовать это для реализации логической функции, нужно запрограммировать её, пережигая перемычки (фьюзы), которые являются связями внутри чипа. Оставляются нужные связи и пережигаются ненужные.

Оно принадлежит к тому же семейству устройств, что и ULA (Uncommitted Logic Array), название которой, в свете предыдущих замечаний, говорит само за себя.

Это блок обобщенной логики, который в своем девственном состоянии не привязан ни к какой конкретной функции. Его нужно запрограммировать для выполнения определенной задачи. Эти устройства могут заменить целую связку вентилей и триггеров и привносят возможность программирования в проектирование дискретной логики.

Надеюсь, это проясняет ситуацию. Это предмет, о котором я много знаю, так как я инженер-конструктор электроники, и я потратил много лет на разработку схем и систем для электронного управления в автоматизации и измерительной технике.

Сейчас я безработный, и поскольку я почти пенсионного возраста, это вряд ли изменится. Однако я развлекаю себя и поддерживаю мозг в тонусе с помощью моего Spectrum.

Он начинался как 16K, но теперь имеет 48K, нормальную клавиатуру и нормальный блок питания — те две области, на которых экономили. Решив эти вопросы, я нахожу его очень полезной машиной. Кроме того, я использую Betabasic, который превращает его в первоклассный аппарат.

Я использую его для игр с кодом Z80 и написания программ для анализа цепей и математики, что является моими главными интересами.

Хотя я был связан с компьютерами так или иначе, от их проектирования до использования в системах, с 1960 года, у меня никогда не было своего, пока я не получил Spectrum. Я пробовал другие машины, но всегда возвращался к мнению, что могу делать все, что хочу, на том, что у меня есть.

Возвращаясь к вопросу о программаторе PAL, технически было бы возможно разработать его на базе Spectrum так же, как существовали разработки программаторов PROM, но могу с достаточной уверенностью сказать, что этого не было сделано, так как, думаю, я бы об этом слышал.

Я баловался идеей создания обучающих программ по логическому проектированию вместе с методом моделирования логики, тем самым доказывая её работоспособность перед сборкой. Я думал, что при всей нынешней «шумихе» вокруг IBM и распространенном среди большинства мнении, что Spectrum — это детская игрушка, никто не воспримет такое всерьез. Однако, похоже, существует прослойка пользователей, которые признают хорошую вещь, когда видят её.

        Искренне ваш,
